main_body: Shrine building with copper-green roof, red timber frame, plaster walls, and lattice doors
top_band: copper-green sloped roof and ridge from row 4 to 42
evidence: The building shows a prominent sloped copper-green roof surface (rows 4-42, 39 rows tall) sitting above a red lintel beam (rows 43-45) with dark eave/beam shadows (row 46-47) over the recessed plaster wall and dark lattice doors (rows 47-73).

style.evidence: The roof has 5 distinct teal/green tones with vertical ribbed tiling, and the outlines use dark tinted material tones (dark brown on timber, dark teal on roof). However, compared to the Beodeul reference buildings which have dense, multi-tone plaster speckles and detailed per-tile roof patterns, the candidate's plaster walls are mostly a single flat cream fill with sparse, faint 1-step dots, and the red timber beams are long unvaried horizontal/vertical bands.
